subject: Logic
title: Brain in a Vat
description: One-minute skill: Brain in a Vat.

hook.text: What if your brain is sitting in a jar, fed perfect simulated experiences by a supercomputer? How would you know?

buildup.text: Hilary Putnam modernized Descartes' evil demon into this scenario to probe the limits of knowledge.

discovery.text: If the simulation is perfect, no experience could distinguish real from fake. Every test would pass.

twist.text: Putnam argued you can't coherently refer to a real vat if you've never encountered one. The hypothesis defeats itself.

climax.text: The experiment doesn't prove we're not in a vat. It shows the question may be unanswerable—or meaningless.

punchline.text: If you can't tell, does the difference matter?

quiz.question: What does the brain-in-a-vat scenario challenge?
options: Whether we can know our experiences are real
